    Dragonreach¶

    "Either we die in glory or live to see another day under honor." — Plenio, Diana, and Korvald, before entering Dragonreach

    The Dragonreach mountains stretch across western Erisdar, forming a natural spine from the northern coasts of Kille down through Augagarten and into the wildlands south of Matterbleak. The peaks are ancient — worn smooth by wind and ice — but it is not their age that makes them feared. It is what lives inside them.

    Dragonreach was the capital of Klobiendar, the dragon empire of West Erisdar that rivaled Xi, the dragon kingdom of the east. It is now a graveyard.

    The Draconic War¶

    The Draconic War pitted Klobiendar against Xi — two dragon empires, millions of soldiers, fifty years of slaughter. Billions died. In the final act, Melberior, the dragon leader of Xi, launched a suicide spell that destroyed Klobiendar's capital entirely. Melberior died in the casting. The magic was so immense that it reverberated across the land, creating the Lyrical Forest above Dragonreach — the souls of the fallen, the echo of the war, still humming in the trees.

    Fallen Dragons¶

    Dragonreach is full of Fallen Dragons — half-alive, half-dead, similar to the entity in the Ruins of Baoth. They are not exactly conscious. They are not exactly dead. They can speak. They are usually violent unless a person proves worthy of their respect.

    The most prominent of them is Fireborn — former dragon king of Klobiendar, father of Goldenborn, now a Fallen Dragon who still holds court in the deepest chambers of the mountain.

    Adventurers attempt to enter Dragonreach. Most meet their demise. The few who survive speak of caverns that descend deeper than the mountains rise, of circling shapes in the dark that watch without attacking, and of a presence that judges before it kills.

    Julian the Dragon Tamer¶

    See: Julian the Dragon Tamer

    In 528 BGD, a man named Julian entered Dragonreach. His family had been murdered by a Shadow-possessed aristocrat from Baoth. He came seeking them back. He found Fireborn instead.

    After a ten-hour duel — in which Julian lost an arm, most of his teeth, and his face was disfigured, yet kept fighting until he reached one centimeter from Fireborn's core of life — Fireborn acknowledged him as the prophet. Fireborn spilled the black agent onto Julian, restoring his body. He gave Julian the Sword of Xi and told him the truth: the Hybrians had come to Ge'or to destroy all families — and Julian's was their victim.

    Julian's story ended at his family's grave, where he touched their bodies, heard their voices telling him to rest, and died on the spot. His corpse disintegrated into the black agent. Fireborn flew above Baoth and consumed his disintegrating form. Julian incarnated into Fireborn — and learned he must wait for two prophets yet to come, whom he must test and prove.

    Treasure & Danger¶

    The Sword of Xi fell during the chaos in Baoth. Anyone who tried to hold it immediately died. A monument was built around it — those ruins still stand in the Ruins of Baoth, and the sword remains in the ground at that exact location.

    Dragonreach itself holds many more treasures for those who are brave. Fireborn's words: "Many more treasures are held in Dragonreach for those that are brave." Treasure hunters from Augamouth and Astravayne still disappear into the caves. Few return.
